summary: GLP-1 radar for Oct 15, 2026. Three things lead this snapshot. (1) Bootleg "Reta" retatrutide. CBS News reported 2 deaths submitted to FDA's adverse event reporting system (FAERS); the FDA has not verified them, and no one has shown the drug caused them. Poison-centre reports are also climbing. This matches our proven myth-bust format about online or unapproved drugs (56 views), and the "when can I get retatrutide?" searches are spiking next to it. (2) Retatrutide's TRIUMPH-2 Phase 3 trial in type 2 diabetes. Lilly reported up to 18.8% weight loss at 80 weeks and plans to file with the FDA in Q1 2027. That fits our "named next-gen drug" decoder format. (3) Orforglipron (Foundayo) vs oral semaglutide in ACHIEVE-3. This is a head-to-head comparison of two pills with clear numbers, and it fits our pills lane. A longevity story is also getting mainstream pickup (CNN, NewsNation, Novo/Lilly claims about living 2–3 more years), but it needs careful framing. Lean on the SELECT/SURPASS-CVOT trial data and avoid anti-aging language. Steady-demand topics refreshed by new hooks: keeping results after stopping (pilot RCT plus Business Insider and Medical News Today), pregnancy (a new 2.1M-pregnancy analysis plus an international consensus), surgery ("tell your team"), and alcohol (an RCT plus a new 1,200-person trial). Safety-scare items (vision loss/NAION, nails) are covered last and only with calm framing, because our data shows they land below median. Psoriasis (TOGETHER-PsO) is fading across snapshots and has been dropped. Plague is out of scope.

candidates.topic: Bootleg 'Reta' (online 'retatrutide'): 2 deaths reported to FDA's FAERS, unverified and causation not established, while poison-centre calls rise
candidates.angle: Calm myth-bust: 'Is online "Reta" the same as Lilly's retatrutide? No.' Retatrutide is investigational and not approved anywhere as of Oct 2026. Lilly has reported finding suspect products with 'too much, too little, or the wrong active ingredient'. The FAERS death reports are unverified and causation isn't established; say that plainly. Close with: real access to new medicines goes through trials and prescribers. Never name sellers or say how to buy.
candidates.why_now: CBS investigation (Oct 13), then NewsNation, MedPage Today, Gizmodo (Oct 14) and Medical Daily on poison-centre calls. Search-style headlines ('what is reta') are multiplying. Mainstream pickup has started, but creator explainers that stay accurate are still thin. It matches our proven online-retatrutide myth-bust Short (56 views).

candidates.topic: Can GLP-1 medicines help people live longer? What the outcome trials show (SELECT, SURPASS-CVOT) vs the 'anti-aging' headlines
candidates.angle: Decoder: 'Novo and Lilly say these drugs could add years. Here's what's measured and what's modelled.' Measured: outcome trials in specific populations, such as SELECT (adults with heart disease plus overweight/obesity, without diabetes) and SURPASS-CVOT (tirzepatide vs dulaglutide in T2D, 16% lower all-cause death reported). Modelled or early: the '2–3 years' estimates and proteomic 'organ age'. Experts say it's too early to take these drugs just to live longer. No anti-aging hashtags.
